items.title: Palworld publishing chief worries early access has 'lost its meaning' as the rise of 'hyper-casual' gaming culture means people often don't understand what they're getting into
items.summary: "People just buy an early access game like they buy a normal game and treat it like that's the game."
items.body: Early access on Steam is a simple concept. You buy a game before it's finished, provide bug reports and feedback to developers, and help shape a project's direction and ambitions. Everybody wins: You get to play the game early, and developers earn money that helps them continue and finish their work. It's been a boon for numerous notable games over the years, including Baldur's Gate 3 and Palworld . In an interview with GamesRadar , though, Pocketpair communications and publishing chief John Buckley said that proposition is becoming increasingly difficult for developers, because the whole idea of early access has "lost its meaning." "Go back to the Steam Greenlight days, when Steam changed Greenlight to early access, there were a few years where it really was running and operating exactly the way I think Steam dreamed it," Buckley said. "I think everyone knew what they were in for. The kind of people who were buying early access games knew what they were in for. They were the kind of gamers who want to be involved, they want to give feedback, they want to talk to devs. It was this really beautiful golden era." items.title: Thief designer thinks the graphics arms race should have ended with 2010's Alan Wake: 'The fidelity curve has become outrageous'
items.summary: "Why do we need more graphics? Because they just cost a ton."
items.body: Thief designer Randy Smith Evergreen, whose credits also include System Shock 2 and Dark Messiah: Might and Magic, thinks we need to chill out a bit when it comes to the graphics arms race. Specifically, he reckons the race should have stopped 16 years ago with Remedy's original Alan Wake, which was quite a looker back in the day. "The fidelity curve has become outrageous," he tells us. "It's become a spectacle. I remember it was back when Alan Wake came out that I was like, 'OK, this is relatively photoreal. I know 100% that I'm on a ferry. I see that I'm going to an island in the Pacific Northwest. Why do we need more graphics? Because they just cost a ton.' Like, I 100% get it. I've got the vibe. It feels right. What else are we doing with this graphics arms race, right?" Quite a lot, it turns out. We had high-fidelity graphics that started to look photorealistic, but then it was decided that we needed lighting and reflections that looked better than real. items.title: Koorui G2741L review
items.summary: Smart compromises make for a punchy monitor on a budget.
items.body: Dual-mode is still not perfect in gaming monitors, but we are consistently getting the option for nearly no extra cost, and that is making it a mighty viable choice, especially if you are running a rig that can only sometimes run the native resolution. The option to flit from 1080p at double the refresh rate for competitive or highly intensive games, and then back to 4K for lush sights or just a clean desktop in only a few seconds, and with native resolutions, makes so much sense to me. Koorui manages to offer both dual-mode and aggressive 4K pricing at the same time. It's been more than a year since our review, but the Asus ROG Strix XG27UCG , which sits as our pick for the best budget 4K gaming monitor , is $100 more and offers almost identical specs. That's a few ticks in my book already. But stats don't tell you absolutely everything; I've had this Koorui gaming monitor planted on my desk for a few weeks, and I was pleasantly surprised by it. items.title: TSMC continues to rake it in from the 'multi-year AI megatrend,' making a record-breaking $16.35 billion in August alone
items.summary: Is the bubble too big to pop?
items.body: For those who've been sleeping under a cool, mossy rock for the last while, TSMC is the biggest semiconductor manufacturer in the world. You can imagine how well they've been doing as the AI industry races to build more and more data centres—but you also don't need to imagine because the official numbers are in, revealing that TSMC's revenue in August surged by a face-melting year-on-year increase of 53%. TSMC's revenue for August alone totalled NT$514.806 billion , which is roughly $16.35 billion USD. Though this is the first time monthly revenue has broken the NT$500 billion sound barrier, it also marks the fourth consecutive month of record-breaking gains for the company. Between January to August 2026, TSMC made NT$3,386.87 billion (roughly $117 billion USD). This in itself is a 39.3% year-on-year increase. CEO C.C. Wei said during the company's latest earnings call that "AI-related demand continues to be extremely robust. The AI megatrend continues to drive the need for more and more computation, which supports the robust demand for leading-edge silicon. items.title: You can now apply DLSS 5 to your entire desktop with a free app and it even works with RTX 30-series cards
items.summary: That includes doing the neural rendering dance all over videos and photos.
items.body: DLSS 5 has been a contentious ol' bit of tech, but with it launching in NBA 2K27 , it's finally in actual games and not just in a ton of ReShade modded games . If, for some reason, you just really love the look, it turns out you can apply it to your entire desktop too, with a little bit of modding help. Posted to GitHub by Perseval BLR, DLSS 5 NeuralScreen is free to download, and it has customisation features to change intensity and swap resolution on the fly (Via TweakTown ). Interestingly, it works with RTX 30-series cards and up. To get it running, you simply have to download the latest version of the app via the GitHub releases tab and run the exe file. You may be wondering why you would bother applying DLSS Neural Rendering to your entire desktop, especially when you consider that a screenshot of a DLSS 5 game as your wallpaper would be less intensive than running an app on it, and the answer is: for everyday use. You can apply DLSS NR while watching videos if you want to, you can apply it to any pictures you open up, and it will even run on any games that you run in borderless or windowed mode. items.body: "الزعيم" يبدأ عصرًا جديدًا اختار نادي الهلال السعودي أول رؤسائه في حقبة الأمير الوليد بن طلال، مالكه الجديد، بعد إتمام الاستحواذ عليه من شركة المملكة القابضة. ونشر نادي الهلال، عبر موقعه الرسمي، بيانًا كشف فيه عن اختيار الأمير نواف بن سعد رئيسًا لمجلس شركة النادي، ليُكمل مسيرته التي بدأت منذ العام الماضي، على أن يكون نائبه هو عبدالمجيد بن أحمد الحقباني. وجاء هذا القرار بعدما عقدت الجمعية العامة لشركة نادي الهلال، اليوم الخميس، اجتماعها الأول بعد اكتمال استحواذ شركة المملكة القابضة على 70% من أسهمها بشكل رسمي. وبالإضافة إلى الرئيس ونائبه، كشف الهلال عن تعيين ياسر بن سليمان الداود، ونواف بن بندر التمياط، وعادل بن عبدالعزيز العبدالسلام، وخالد بن رفيق كريديه، كأعضاء في مجلس إدارة شركة النادي. وكانت شركة المملكة القابضة، المملوكة للأمير الوليد بن طلال، قد وقعت على اتفاقية ملزمة مع صندوق الاستثمارات العامة السعودي، للاستحواذ على 70% من أسهم الهلال، في أبريل/نيسان الماضي، قبل إتمام الاستحواذ بشكل رسمي الأسبوع الماضي.

As explained on the CWA website , this contract has been in the works for two years and impacts around 1900 workers from across the studio, including those working on World of Warcraft , Hearthstone, QA, Overwatch, and Diablo. The contract itself does a lot of good for these people, who are living in an era of uncertainty thanks to Xbox's 'reset' that has impacted over 1600 jobs and is soon to jeopardise 1600 more. items.title: Nvidia is reportedly being investigated by the DOJ over its biggest ever deal, a $20 billion non-exclusive agreement with Groq
items.summary: Apparently the deal might have been structured to avoid the usual automatic scrutiny.
items.body: At the back end of 2025, Nvidia secured its biggest ever deal, a $20 billion non-exclusive agreement with AI chip company Groq . Now, as reported by the New York Times , per "two people with knowledge of the inquiry", the Department of Justice (DOJ) is probing to discover whether the deal was organised in a way that would get around antitrust scrutiny. If found at fault, the people say, Nvidia could be fined. The original agreement gives Nvidia non-exclusive rights to Groq tech, namely AI chips that are good for low-latency inference. The first Nvidia AI rack featuring Groq chips is said to go live later this year . According to the NYT, one of the two people with knowledge of the inquiry claims the DOJ has sent Nvidia a formal demand for information about the Groq deal. The issue appears to be one that is somewhat common in the AI industry: deals that are framed not as acquisitions but as licensing agreements. Apparently having the deals structured like this can evade automatic government reviews. The two sources cited in the NY Times piece requested anonymity on the grounds that the process itself is confidential, and also noted that there has currently been no specific findings…

items.body: While I've largely enjoyed any time I've dipped a toe into virtual reality, I definitely do not own a VR headset. As cool as the tech is, that hardware remains an expensive niche within the increasingly pricey PC gaming landscape. Global VR headset shipments apparently declined by 18% year-on-year in the second quarter of 2026, according to the latest data from Counterpoint Research . That doesn't surprise me—though it's also not great news for Valve or the potentially imminent release of its Steam Frame VR headset. items.body: Three months ago, Corsair announced the TC80 gaming chair . At the time, I was pretty excited for it, because it (A) strips back the overly-gamefied stylings and (B) is, according to Corsair, "affordable." Back then we didn't have the price, but now we do . It's going to cost just $200/£170/€180, though this is "subject to change." For context, that's $50 cheaper than our current pick for the best budget gaming chair , the ThunderX3 Solo 360 . Of course we don't know how nice this Corsair will be to actually sit on yet, but the old Corsair TC100 Relaxed was our pick as best budget chair for a real long time, and it's good to see a mainstream brand continuing to push for something so affordable compared to the $500–$600 'premium' options we've become used to seeing. Corsair explains all the different kinds of durability and stability testing the chair has gone through, which gives me some level of confidence in it. The tests include dropping 136 kg onto the seat, as well as applying lots of force to different parts of the chair, plenty of times.
